title: Non-Standard Marker Comments
pattern: Temporary developer note denoting incomplete work or issues, written using non-standard symbols instead of standardized compiler/linter tags.
why_bad: Fails mechanical tool lookup. Arbitrary strings cannot be indexed by compilers, IDEs, or automated CI release checklists, leading to incomplete code slipping into production.
detection: Inline comments containing indicators like 'NEED TO', 'FIX', 'TBD', 'NOT DONE', or heavy punctuation (e.g., '!!!', '***') that do not conform to standard parser tags (`TODO` or `FIXME`).
counterexample: Standardized `// TODO:` or `// FIXME:` tags that IDEs, linters, and CI checklists can index mechanically.
fix: Convert to standard `// TODO:` or `// FIXME:` format.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32.4 ("Marker in the Code").
